name: Museo Amparo
funding: Fundación Amparo, set up by banker Manuel Espinosa Yglesias, funds the museum.
watch: Name to know: FEMSA. Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas marched in April 2017 to cancel Coca-Cola FEMSA's water concession.
why_flagged: Name to know: FEMSA. Residents of San Cristóbal de las Casas marched in April 2017 to cancel Coca-Cola FEMSA's water concession.
records_note: Owner Fundación Amparo posts a 2025 activities report; neither site shows accounts, donors or a board, only a staff directory.

name: Fundación Casa Wabi
funding: Artist-founded non-profit (Bosco Sodi, 2014); 2026 sponsors: Harp Helú, Home Depot, Teka, Grupo Habita, Tequila 1800, Punta Pájaros, Nirox Foundation.
watch: Supporter roster unverified. Allowed money named: alcohol (Tequila 1800), retail (Home Depot), hotels/property (Grupo Habita, Punta Pájaros), banking family (Harp Helú).
records_note: Casa Wabi thanks its sponsors with an undated page of logos and lists staff directors, but posts no annual reports, accounts or board.

name: Museo de Arte de Zapopan
watch: Free public contemporary art museum. The old domain mazmuseo.com now carries casino spam links; the municipal site is maz.zapopan.gob.mx.
records_note: The municipal museum's site lists exhibitions, programmes and a contact address, with no annual reports, accounts, sponsor names or board.

name: Fondation Ifitry
funding: Run under Maroc Premium Foundation, which has overseen the Casablanca Biennale and the Essaouira art centre since 2014. No funder list is published.
watch: Artist residency near Essaouira founded in 2008 by Mostapha Romli. The ifitry.ma site no longer resolves.
records_note: It has no site of its own; its parent biennale shows 2021 partner logos without names, with no reports, accounts or board.

name: Museum Arnhem
funding: Run by Stichting Musea Arnhem since 2014 on an annual Gemeente Arnhem subsidy (€2.6M in 2011).
watch: Reopened on 13 May 2022 after a delayed renovation. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: Museum Arnhem posts annual reports for 2012 to 2024, links full accounts, names its supervisory board, and names six funds undated.

name: Fries Museum
funding: Provinsje Fryslân gives fixed subsidy; OCW and VriendenLoterij support; Windpark Fryslân is a named partner, with Fonds 21, Mondriaan Fonds, Cultuurfonds, VSBfonds, Turing and Wetterskip Fryslân.
watch: Director Kris Callens left in February 2025; the museum cited transgressive behaviour. ING and ABN AMRO are not on the current partners page.
records_note: The Fries Museum posts annual reports for 2003 to 2024, links full accounts on an ANBI site, names partners undated, and lists its supervisory board.

name: Museum De Lakenhal
funding: Gemeente Leiden, Province of South Holland and OCW fund it. Its thanks page also names BankGiro Lottery, Mondriaan Fonds, Ammodo, BNG Cultuurfonds, VSBfonds and Fonds 21.
watch: The thanks page lists all donors since founding, including the tobacco-family Niemeijer Fonds, undated, so it is not counted. No protest found.
records_note: De Lakenhal posts annual reports for 2007 to 2025 that name its funds and partners, but shows no accounts and no board list.

name: Nederlands Fotomuseum
funding: Ministry of OCW and Gemeente Rotterdam give annual support. Droom en Daad funded the Santos warehouse; the Wertheimer legacy, Fonds 21, Rabobank Rotterdam Fonds and others add project money.
watch: Droom en Daad (Van der Vorm family) bought the Santos warehouse. Boijmans refused its €80M offer in 2019 after it asked for two board seats.
why_flagged: Droom en Daad (Van der Vorm family) bought the Santos warehouse. Boijmans refused its €80M offer in 2019 after it asked for two board seats.
records_note: It posts annual reports for 2018 to 2025 with audited accounts, a named 2025 funder appendix, ANBI forms and a named supervisory board.

name: Museum Beelden aan Zee
watch: The researcher's BNG, Aegon and other names come from 2018 and 2019 reports, so they are not current. BNG is state-owned; no protest found.
records_note: Its ANBI page posts annual reports 2017 to 2024, yearly accounts 2012 to 2025 and a named board; the 2024 report names about 30 funders.

name: Centraal Museum
watch: The page gives no amounts or dates for the three. No protest or censorship found.
records_note: It posts annual reports and accounts for 2018 to 2025 and a named supervisory board; the 2025 report lists funders and corporate partners by name.

name: Te Uru Waitakere Contemporary Gallery
funding: Core funding from the Waitākere Ranges Local Board (Auckland Council). It also takes gifts from a Benefactors Collective and sponsors, none named.
watch: Income was NZ$1.17M in the year to June 2024.
records_note: No annual reports on its site; the NZ register holds returns to June 2024. One council funder is named; the About page lists the board.

name: Dunedin Public Art Gallery
funding: Dunedin City Council gallery. Gallery Partners are Creative New Zealand, Quartz Reef and Craigs Investment Partners; the DPAG Society buys works.
watch: Founding partners in 1996 included Mobil Oil New Zealand and the Lotteries Board; neither is a current funder.
records_note: A council unit with no reports or accounts of its own. Its supporters page names gallery partners and benefactors; staff are listed, no board.
